transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 14:30 PST
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Aisha Khan (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Dr. Maya Patel (CTO, Orthosys), Jordan Reyes (Head of MLOps), Samir Gupta (Security)

[00:00] Aisha: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — hi Maya, Jordan, Samir — can you hear us ok?
[00:04] Maya: Yep, loud and clear. Thanks Aisha.
[00:06] Jordan: All good here.
[00:10] Aisha: Awesome. Today we'll run through Redwood's model catalog — how you pick open models, the benchmark data we surface, and the compatibility matrix for Dedicated/Hosted/Private. Liam will dive into the Console and API. We'll leave time for Q&A and then recap next steps.
[01:00] Liam: Quick note — we'll reference the benchmark spreadsheet and the compatibility matrix in the deck, link is in chat: https://redwood.ai/docs/model-catalog and I've also uploaded the perf sheet (link).
[02:20] Samir: Thanks — from security side, we'll need SOC2, SAML/SSO details, KMS integration, and audit log retention info. Also curious about on-prem options for PHI.
[02:50] Aisha: Absolutely. We have SOC2 and ISO artifacts, and Private deployment supports customer-managed KMS and audit logs. We'll share the docs after the call.
[03:15] Liam: Ok jumping into the catalog — home screen shows curated open models with performance profiles. Each model card has throughput, median latency for common sequence lengths, quantization compatibility, and hardware preference (A100, H100, etc).
[03:45] Maya: Are those latency numbers from our own runs or community?
[03:50] Liam: Mostly Redwood-verified benchmarks on standard workloads; for some community models we show a note that numbers are best-effort. There's also a compatibility matrix that maps model variants to runtime paths — e.g., 8-bit quantization supported, KV-cache optimizations enabled, and which kernel backends we use.
[04:30] Jordan: When you say compatibility matrix, is it per-model-version? We maintain pinned versions for inference.
[04:40] Liam: Yes per-version. The matrix indicates e.g. gpt-neoX-20b:v1 -> supports int8, works on H100 with cutlass kernels, recommended for long-context use because of our optimized KV cache. Note: sometimes transcribed as K-V cash in the UI, heh.
[05:15] Maya: We run mostly 2–4k token contexts for summarization pipelines. Target p95 latency is 300ms for single-turn calls.
[05:30] Aisha: Good context. That helps pick model and deployment: hosted may hit latency sometimes depending on burst and region; Dedicated gives predictable throughput and lower p95s.
[06:00] Liam: Demonstrating the Console — search by capability (summarization), filter by max latency, cost per 1k tokens estimate, and whether model is compatible with private deployment. Click into a model to see the benchmark tab that includes sequences (512/1024/4096), throughput, and cost estimates under different batching policies.
[07:00] Jordan: How deterministic are the cost estimates? We have strict budget constraints.
[07:10] Liam: Estimates are based on our measured tokens/sec on targeted hardware and a pricing layer; when you run a pilot we'll produce a usage forecast given your profile. Also Optimize recommends batch sizes and quantization levels to hit your cost/latency target.
[07:50] Maya: Can we force fallback to a smaller model during spikes? We want graceful degradation.
[07:57] Liam: Yes — Smart routing supports fallback policies. You can set a tiered policy: hosted -> dedicated -> smaller variant; or region fallback. We'll show that in the routing tab.
[08:30] Samir: For PHI, encryption at rest and in transit are musts. How do you handle key management?
[08:38] Aisha: For Private deployments we can integrate with your KMS/HSM. For Dedicated we offer customer-managed KMS integrations in the private plane. We'll include the KMS integration guide in the doc packet.
[09:10] Jordan: Any limitations on model quantization? We run some custom finetunes.
[09:16] Liam: Our catalog lists quantization compatibility per model-version. Some finetunes break symmetric quantization, so we recommend re-quantizing with Redwood Optimize or shipping a quantization profile. If you're using custom finetunes, we can run a quick validation as part of the pilot.
[10:05] Maya: Show us an example — pick a model for summarization and walk through API call.
[10:10] Liam: Sure. Selecting 'open-summarizer-14b:v2' — click "Use in API". Example request shows model name, max_tokens, temperature, and routing: "region: us-west-2, preference: lowest-latency, fallback: open-summarizer-6b".
[11:00] Liam: Note the streaming support and the function/tool calling examples — for structured outputs we expose a JSON schema enforcement option.
[11:40] Jordan: We use node SDKs and have a serverless front end — any cold start concerns?
[11:48] Aisha: Prefetching and warmup policies help; Dedicated avoids runtime cold starts for GPU pools. Optimize can suggest prewarming windows based on traffic patterns.
[12:30] Liam: Back to benchmark sheet — for 4k context, open-summarizer-14b:v2 on H100 with int8 showed median token latency of ~12ms/token in our tests, which maps to ~200–250ms per 4k request depending on output length and batching. For throughput, a 3-GPU Dedicated pool at x throughput will handle ~Y qps for 1–2k token prompts. (numbers are illustrative; we'll run a tailored benchmark).
[13:40] Samir: You mentioned kernel backends — are those based on Triton or custom kernels?
[13:45] Liam: Mix of both — we use custom optimized kernels for attention and KV cache, and fall back to vendor libraries when appropriate. The compatibility table flags which backend is used per model/hardware.
[14:20] Maya: How do you surface regression monitoring? We need quality monitoring post-deploy.
[14:27] Liam: The Console has evals integration — you can attach prompt sets, baseline outputs, and get alerts on distributional shifts or regression in scores. There's also an A/B rollout tool to compare model variants.
[15:10] Jordan: For the pilot, we'd like to run hosted first then move traffic to Dedicated if latency promises meet our SLO. What does that timeline look like?
[15:20] Aisha: Typical is 2 weeks for a small pilot: week 1 onboarding + baseline tests, week 2 dedicated perf runs and rollout planning. We'll provide a runbook and a benchmark template.
[16:05] Liam: Quick demo: Console -> Model -> Benchmarks. (screen share) See the compatibility matrix — some community models are flagged: "experimental int8" or "not supported for private deployments". You can export the matrix as CSV.
[17:30] Maya: If we have custom finetunes, can Redwood host the finetuned artifact? Where does the model live?
[17:38] Liam: For Hosted and Dedicated the weights are stored in our artifact store with encryption; for Private we can store on your infra or support bringing your own artifact. We'll share the model onboarding guide for custom artifacts.
[18:15] Samir: Audit logs and retention — can we set retention windows? Also need searchable event logs for compliance.
[18:23] Aisha: Yes, audit logs configurable; we'll include the retention policy options and pricing for extended retention. Searchable logs via the Console are supported for enterprise tiers.
[19:00] Jordan: Any callouts about data residency for EU customers?
[19:06] Liam: We can pin regions and ensure data never leaves a region for Private deployments; hosted API can be region-restricted too.
[19:45] Maya: Benchmarks — when you run them, do you use our workload shapes or synthetic?
[19:50] Liam: We run both. We start with synthetic standardized tests for apples-to-apples, then run your anonymized samples for realistic numbers. We'll need a small sample dataset (no PHI ideally) or sanitized versions.
[20:30] Jordan: For cost optimization, you mentioned quantization profiles and batching. How much can we expect to save?
[20:37] Liam: Typical 8-bit quantization yields 2–3x token throughput improvement with small quality delta; combined with batching and caching, unit cost can drop 30–60% depending on workload. Optimize recommends a profile per model+workload.
[21:25] Samir: Can you guarantee model outputs are not cached in ways that violate PHI policies?
[21:30] Aisha: We support controls to disable persistent caching for sensitive workloads and allow you to configure prefix only caching or disable KV persistence.
[22:00] Maya: Ok let's talk about metrics for our pilot — target p95 <300ms for 2–4k contexts on main summarizer path, end-to-end availability 99.9, and cost per 1k tokens under $X (we'll provide target).
[22:18] Aisha: Noted. We'll add those to the runbook and put a custom ops play for routing and fallbacks.
[23:00] Liam: Quick note on SDKs — Node, Python, and Java SDKs have identical interfaces for model naming and routing. Example: redwood.models.create({model: 'open-summarizer-14b:v2', routing: {preference: 'latency'}})
[24:00] Maya: Any known gotchas moving from hosted to Dedicated?
[24:05] Liam: Mostly capacity planning — Dedicated pools need sizing and a brief setup window; autoscaling policies are configurable. Also if you bring finetuned weights there may be additional validation time.
[25:20] Jordan: For our internal procurement, we'll need a security questionnaire filled and an NDA.
[25:28] Aisha: We'll send the security pack and a draft MSA.
[26:00] (brief side conversation, inaudible)
[27:10] Samir: One more security question — SSO integration, do you support SCIM provisioning?
[27:16] Liam: Yes, we support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning for user management. We'll share the SSO implementation guide.
[28:05] Maya: Can we run a short benchmark now? Even a small sanity check?
[28:10] Liam: We can run a quick lightweight request from the hosted endpoint with a short prompt — won't reflect Dedicated numbers but good for smoke test. (runs live demo)
[29:00] [small pause, network noise]
[29:12] Liam: Response came back — streamed, example output shown. Note that hosted latency was ~120ms for the short prompt.
[30:00] Maya: Noted. We'll still want Dedicated numbers for the 4k flows.
[30:20] Aisha: Recap of next steps: we'll send pricing, SOC2/SAML/KMS docs, and the benchmark template. Liam will provision the runbook and sample scripts; Jordan will share sanitized data. Plan kickoff for week of 3/9.
[31:00] Jordan: Sounds good. Any blockers on our side?
[31:04] Samir: Need to confirm legal/ procurement timeline but otherwise ok.
[31:20] Maya: Also confirm whether exports of audit logs are supported for SIEM ingestion.
[31:28] Liam: Yes, we have export connectors; we'll include the details.
[32:15] Aisha: Ok thanks everyone. We'll email the packet today and follow up with proposed pilot schedule.
[32:25] Maya: Thank you.
[32:30] Jordan: Thanks.
[32:32] Samir: Thanks all.
[32:40] Aisha: Bye everyone.

(End of recording)
